parsed.draft_response:
Hi—thanks for flagging this. We’re treating this as a potential security/access-control issue and have escalated it for human review.

To help our security team investigate whether any cross-tenant access (or data exposure) actually occurred, could you share a few details?
1) Product/service and environment (cloud/region, deployment type, tenant/workspace identifiers if you can share them safely).
2) Exact steps to reproduce: how the report link is created, how/where it’s forwarded, and what the receiving workspace/user does when accessing it.
3) What the receiving workspace can do after following the link (e.g., does it only open a page/link, or can it load specific report contents/underlying data?).
4) Any evidence you have already collected: audit logs, request IDs, timestamps/time window, screenshots, or traces showing the cross-tenant behavior.
5) Scope and impact: how many users/workspaces/tenants are potentially affected, and whether you’ve confirmed this is ongoing.
6) Any mitigations already attempted (e.g., link revocation, disabling sharing, access control changes).

In the meantime, if you still have the affected shared links, please avoid further sharing and consider restricting access/revoking the specific links (if your workflow supports that) while we review.

We’ll follow up as soon as the security team completes the initial assessment. If you can provide the reproduction steps and any available logs/request IDs, that will help us move faster.
promised_actions: Escalate the report for security/human review
Follow up after an initial assessment once additional details and evidence are provided
safety_notes: Do not claim confirmation of cross-tenant access or exfiltration
Do not promise a specific fix or refund
Ask for minimum useful clarification: environment, repro steps, what recipient can access, and supporting evidence (logs/request IDs/timestamps)
